technical_and_design_decisions: Use the existing project build system, module structure, Spring conventions, and supported Java version rather than introducing a parallel architecture.
Treat dependency selection as a deterministic resolution process with explicit version precedence and clear fallback behavior when no binding is configured.
Prefer existing Maven or Spring dependency-resolution infrastructure where compatible; avoid implementing a complete repository or artifact resolver from scratch.
Implement undeploy through a common lifecycle abstraction so the single-node target can apply consistent behavior to both streams and jobs.
Use Spring profiles to select repository and metadata-storage strategies, with a local profile backed by an in-memory implementation.
Expose counter metrics through the application's existing web and management endpoint conventions, using a stable JSON response suitable for dashboard consumption.
Publish a reproducible Docker image from the project build and configure incremental publishing to DockerHub through the existing CI mechanism.
Document the XD-to-s-c-s module migration foundation as an architectural design and prototype guidance, not as a full migration of all modules.
assumptions: The existing source repository, build, test infrastructure, and CI configuration are available and can be modified by one developer.
The increment targets the currently supported Java and Spring versions in the repository; no framework-wide upgrade is required.
The existing project already has usable abstractions for bindings, modules, streams, jobs, repositories, and the single-node runtime.
Dependency resolution is limited to the runtime module and binding scenarios described in the stories; arbitrary native-library conflicts and full classloader isolation are out of scope.
The selected dependency-resolution behavior can use existing Maven, Spring, or classloader facilities rather than requiring a new artifact repository service.
Undeploy must stop and remove a running single-node stream or job using the existing runtime process model; distributed deployment targets are out of scope.
The local profile's in-memory metadata strategy does not need persistence across process restarts.
The counter endpoint can be implemented using the existing HTTP management layer, and authentication, authorization, and long-term metrics storage are out of scope.
DockerHub credentials, repository permissions, and CI secrets are available; publishing is limited to the required image and latest-commit workflow.
The screencast uses an existing firehose and counter pipe example, and only preparation, recording, light editing, publication, and documentation are included.
The XD module-porting work produces an architectural foundation, conventions, and one small illustrative prototype rather than porting the complete module catalog.
Estimates include implementation, developer testing, documentation, code review preparation, and local integration validation, but exclude waiting time for external approvals or infrastructure.

activities.activity_description: Inspect the existing modules, runtime lifecycle, binding configuration, dependency management, profile configuration, endpoint layer, build, CI, and test conventions. Produce an implementation map and identify integration points for all user stories.
Investigate how message-bus and binding jars are currently discovered, included, excluded, and selected. Define the no-binding fallback behavior and document the recommended binding-selection design.

Design the runtime dependency-resolution flow for modules that request incompatible jar versions, including version precedence, conflict reporting, fallback behavior, and boundaries between shared and isolated dependencies.
Implement runtime dependency discovery, version conflict handling, selected-artifact inclusion, and integration with module and binding startup using the chosen existing resolution facilities.
Add unit and integration tests covering compatible dependencies, conflicting versions, explicit selections, absent bindings, fallback behavior, and startup failure diagnostics.

activities.activity_name: Docker image build and DockerHub publishing
activities.activity_description: Create or update the reproducible Docker image build, tagging, and CI publishing configuration. Validate image startup locally and verify that latest commits can be pushed to DockerHub.
Prepare the demonstration scenario, run the firehose and counter pipe, record the public screencast, perform light editing, publish it, and add usage links or instructions.

Review the referenced undeploy proposal and existing deployment lifecycle, then define consistent stop, cleanup, state-transition, error, and repeated-operation behavior for single-node streams and jobs.

Implement the single-JVM undeploy operation, including command or API integration, runtime shutdown, metadata cleanup, handling for missing or already-stopped deployments, and shared stream/job lifecycle behavior.
Add unit and integration tests for successful undeploy, stream and job cases, invalid identifiers, repeated undeploy, runtime failures, cleanup, and state consistency.
Define profile activation and configuration rules for the core Admin application, including repository strategy selection, default profile behavior, and extension points for future backends.

Implement profile-aware Admin configuration and the local in-memory metadata repository strategy, wiring it into stream and job operations while preserving existing behavior for other configured backends.
Test profile selection, default behavior, local in-memory storage, repository wiring, isolation between application contexts, and invalid or incomplete configuration.
Review existing XD module patterns and s-c-s module expectations, then design module boundaries, APIs, configuration conventions, packaging, lifecycle, compatibility, and migration sequencing.
Create a small representative prototype or skeleton and document the migration foundation, developer workflow, conventions, risks, and recommended next steps for porting additional modules.
Define the counter metric model, endpoint paths, query or filtering behavior, JSON schema, empty and error responses, and compatibility with the firehose/counter demonstration.
Implement counter collection and HTTP endpoint exposure, connect it to the counter pipe, add serialization and endpoint configuration, and provide the dashboard-consumable response format.
Add unit and web integration tests for counter increments, endpoint responses, empty counters, invalid requests, serialization, and interaction with the demonstration pipeline.
Update configuration references, operational documentation, examples, release notes, and acceptance scenarios. Run the combined firehose/counter, dependency, profile, Docker, and undeploy workflows.
Run the complete test suite, perform focused regression testing across all affected modules, fix integration issues, validate build reproducibility, and prepare the increment for delivery.
